text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Bin Mohammad during his talks with Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has expressed his keenness to initiate joint ventures and remove existing trade imbalance between the two countries.
- The International Monetary Fund has asked Pakistan to disclose the cost of the recently-announced economic reforms but it has set no deadline.
- Pakistan and Singapore have agreed in principle to double the volume of trade between the two countries.
- The government seems to have stepped up its efforts to press feudals in the ruling party to accept levy of farm tax in the coming national budget.
- Italy plans to open its trade office in Karachi by the end of this year.
- Sharif has dismissed two high officials of the Central Board of Revenue responsible for enormous losses to the national exchequer through fraudulent exports.
- The government has decided to import two million tonnes of wheat and 50,000 tonnes of sugar to pre-empt any future crisis.
- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan termed his meeting with his Indian counterpart as congenial and part of an ice-breaking process but said Pakistan would not take any step in isolation.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has recommended to the government to issue bonds worth six billion rupees to banks in lieu of the overdues of Rice Export Corp of Pakistan.
- The Gross Domestic Product is expected to grow by 4.5 percent during 1996/97 (July-June) leading to a budget deficit of six percent.
- Aout two dozen people were wounded when a bomb blast in Gujranwala on Wednesday.
FINANCIAL POST
- The government has allowed the Privatisation Commission to sell the Habib Credit and Exchange Bank.
THE NEWS

- The government has suspended 87 officers, including seven federal secretaries, former and present presidents of state-run banks and former chairman of Pakistan Steel Mills on the charges of corruption.
- A visiting delegation of Audi and Volkswagen group has shown interest in setting up a manufacturing plant for Audi cars in Pakistan.
--Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
